label: E12
headline: First Convoys Transit Meridia Strait as Blockade Framework Holds
body:
OSTREV, Sept. 12 — First commercial convoys moved through the Strait of Meridia in both directions today, marking the first post-decree transits following months of blockade. Tracking data from HarborTrack recorded approximately 50 vessel movements throughout the day, substantially below pre-crisis baseline traffic of roughly 140 commercial ships per day.

The transits occurred under Operation Open Water, the five-nation escort framework comprising Khoreth, Sundaria, Elbar, Aldenport, and Virelles. The Varessan Coastal Forces maintained positioning throughout the strait but did not attempt to interfere with the movements, according to maritime monitors and shipping officials.

"The passage was orderly and protected," said a spokesperson for the Khoreth Maritime Authority. Officials at Qoros Marine Underwriters' Association said no incidents were reported during the day's movements.

Shipping companies expressed cautious optimism about resumption of regular traffic, though the low throughput reflects the operational constraints of convoy assembly and escort coordination. Several trade routes remain under restriction, with captains and brokers continuing to navigate insurance pricing and scheduling amid uncertainty about blockade duration.

The Meridia Route Normalization Index, which reflects market risk assessment, remained significantly depressed, indicating traders do not yet view the transits as establishing stable passage conditions. Additional convoy movements are scheduled through the week.
